task.title: Alert on payment retry bursts
task.description: Operators want an alert when a payment request needs more than 5 retry attempts. Propose the alert and justify the threshold.

task.title: Alert on payment retry bursts
task.description: Operators want an alert when a payment request needs more than 5 retry attempts. Propose the alert and justify the threshold.

proposal.summary: The threshold is taken directly from the operator requirement in the task description. No production retry distribution, retry-policy maximum, baseline rate, or alert-history evidence was provided, so a statistical justification for 5 cannot be claimed from the available evidence; the threshold requires validation against historical data before production paging is relied on.
plan_steps: Define or confirm a per-request retry count derived from retry events grouped by payment request ID.
Implement the alert rule with condition retry_count > 5, severity warning pending operator confirmation, and deduplication by request ID.
Add notification fields listed in claim C3 and link the notification to an operator runbook for retry-burst investigation.
Test the boundary cases 5 and 6 retries and the deduplication case in claims C1, C2, and C4.
Review historical retry distribution, if available, and tune severity, grouping, or rate-based aggregation before enabling production paging.

claims.statement: The alert condition is retry_count > 5 for a single payment request, so it first triggers on the 6th retry attempt for that request.
The alert fires once per request ID on crossing the threshold, rather than once per retry after the threshold.
Each alert notification contains request ID, service name, retry count, first and latest retry timestamps, and downstream error or reason if available.
Alerts at or below 5 retries do not notify operators.
The 5-retry threshold is not validated against normal retry behaviour until baseline data is reviewed.

assumptions: A per-request identifier exists to group retry events for the same payment request.
Retry events or a retry-count metric are emitted by the payment service and are queryable by the alerting system.
uncertainties: Whether 'more than 5 retry attempts' means 6 retries after the initial attempt or 6 total attempts; the proposal interprets it as retry count > 5 and this needs operator confirmation.
What evaluation window, severity, notification channel, and aggregation across many simultaneous requests operators require; not specified in the task.
Whether the existing retry policy already caps retries at or below 5, which would make this alert unreachable unless the cap is higher or bypassed.
What false-positive rate the >5 threshold produces under normal load; no baseline data was provided.

evidence.content: Fact: payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.

items.description: Off-by-one ambiguity unresolved: proposal notes uncertainty whether 'more than 5 retry attempts' means 6 retries after the initial attempt or 6 total attempts, so assertion that it first triggers on the 6th retry is not established.

Potential conflict with retry cap: retrieved constraint 186670067796945807561772405393844769735 asserts retries capped at 3 attempts, which would make retry_count > 5 unreachable, but its integrity is Invalid and the proposal does not verify the actual cap.
No evaluation window, counting method, or handling of duplicate/out-of-order/reset retry events is defined, so retry_count > 5 cannot be reliably implemented or boundary-tested as stated.
Once-per-request deduplication mechanism is unspecified: no crossing-state storage, persistence across evaluation windows/restarts, expiry, or re-arm behaviour is described or tested.

Per-request deduplication does not prevent notification flooding when many distinct request IDs cross simultaneously; no rate aggregation, grouping, or alert-storm test is provided despite this being listed as an open uncertainty.
Claim guarantees downstream error/reason in each notification but qualifies it as 'if available', so field presence is not guaranteed and no test covers its absence.

Security/privacy risk not addressed: request ID and downstream error details sent to a notification channel may expose payment identifiers or internal error data; no redaction, access control, or channel suitability is specified.

Boundary claim depends on unresolved counting interpretation and undefined window/reset semantics; only 5 vs 6 cases are mentioned, with no tests for counts 0-4 across windows, duplicates, or metric resets causing premature/late notification.

Threshold lacks valid support: no baseline distribution was provided and the retrieved fact 8864874238917673930644756936982232317 about bursts above 5 has integrity Invalid, so false-positive rate and paging suitability remain unknown.

Test traceability is broken: plan references claims C1, C2, and C4 but supplied claim ids are claim-2 through claim-6 with no claim-1/C1 definition, so referenced boundary and deduplication coverage cannot be verified.

receipt.proof_limitations: Integrity proofs, where valid, establish that a recalled record matches its anchored snapshot under the memory backend's documented assumptions. They do not establish that the content is true, relevant, or complete, or that a model reasoned from it.
